name: the Schlosspark Nymphenburg
title: Ancient Trees in Nymphenburg Palace Park: 5 Protected
meta_description: Munich protects these five trees by law, and two of them for being strange rather than large: a leaning lime and a beech the city calls bizarre.
intro: Munich protects trees by law here for reasons written down in a city ordinance, and two of these five are protected for being odd rather than big. A large-leaved lime by the Badenburger See is listed as bizarrer und knorriger Wuchs, bizarre and gnarled growth, which is an unusually honest thing for a legal document to say. There is also a weeping beech protected partly because people are fond of it, an oak in the Dorfchen, the part of a royal garden built to look undesigned, and a fern-leaved beech of a form that did not exist anywhere before about 1804.
